content.text: The per-path span names include random IDs, so the join failed. I'll normalise the span names and compare per-service server spans instead.

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT service_name svc, regexp_replace(span_name,'[0-9a-zA-Z]{6,}','X','g') op, attr_span_kind k, count(*)/60.0 rpm, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95, avg(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) err FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2,3), n AS (SELECT service_name svc, regexp_replace(span_name,'[0-9a-zA-Z]{6,}','X','g') op, attr_span_kind k, count(*)/60.0 rpm, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95, avg(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) err FROM normal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2,3) SELECT a.svc, a.op, round(n.rpm,1) n_rpm, round(a.rpm,1) a_rpm, round(n.p95,1) n_p95, round(a.p95,1) a_p95, round(n.err,3) n_err, round(a.err,3) a_err FROM a LEFT JOIN n USING(svc,op,k) ORDER BY a.svc, a.op

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT service_name svc, regexp_replace(span_name,'[0-9a-zA-Z]{6,}','X','g') op, count(*)/60.0 rpm, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95, avg(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) err FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2), n AS (SELECT service_name svc, regexp_replace(span_name,'[0-9a-zA-Z]{6,}','X','g') op, count(*)/60.0 rpm, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95, avg(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) err FROM normal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT a.svc, left(a.op,60) op, round(n.rpm,1) n_rpm, round(a.rpm,1) a_rpm, round(n.p95,1) n_p95, round(a.p95,1) a_p95, round(a.err,3) a_err FROM a LEFT JOIN n USING(svc,op) WHERE a.rpm > 3 ORDER BY a.svc, a.op

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT service_name svc, regexp_replace(span_name,'[0-9a-zA-Z]{6,}','X','g') op, attr_span_kind k, count(*)/60.0 rpm, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95, avg(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) err FROM abnormal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind IN ('Client','Internal') GROUP BY 1,2,3), n AS (SELECT service_name svc, regexp_replace(span_name,'[0-9a-zA-Z]{6,}','X','g') op, attr_span_kind k, count(*)/60.0 rpm, quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6 p95, avg(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) err FROM normal_traces WHERE attr_span_kind IN ('Client','Internal') GROUP BY 1,2,3) SELECT a.svc, left(a.op,70) op, a.k, round(n.rpm,1) n_rpm, round(a.rpm,1) a_rpm, round(n.p95,1) n_p95, round(a.p95,1) a_p95, round(a.err,3) a_err FROM a LEFT JOIN n USING(svc,op,k) WHERE a.rpm > 3 ORDER BY a.svc, a.op

content.text: Food-service's outgoing and internal spans both slowed sharply, and seat-service's client spans are much slower than its callees' server spans. To separate network gap from callee time, I'll join client spans to their child server spans and compare durations.

input.query: WITH pairs AS (SELECT c.service_name caller, s.service_name callee, c.duration cd, s.duration sd, c.attr_status_code cs, s.attr_status_code ss, c.attr_k8s_pod_name cpod, s.attr_k8s_pod_name spod FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client' AND s.attr_span_kind='Server') SELECT caller, callee, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(cd,0.5)/1e6,1) c_p50, round(quantile_cont(sd,0.5)/1e6,1) s_p50, round(quantile_cont(cd,0.95)/1e6,1) c_p95, round(quantile_cont(sd,0.95)/1e6,1) s_p95 FROM pairs GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY (c_p95 - s_p95) DESC LIMIT 25

content.text: The caller-callee gaps are small, so the slowdown is inside the callee services rather than on the wire. Next I'll check metric names and per-service resource shifts for the suspect services.

input.query: SELECT service_name, metric, round(avg(CASE WHEN time < (SELECT min(time) FROM abnormal_metrics)+INTERVAL 1 SECOND THEN NULL END),2) x, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2 LIMIT 1

WITH a AS (SELECT service_name svc, metric, avg(value) av, stddev(value) asd FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('ts-food-service','ts-seat-service','ts-consign-service','ts-preserve-service','ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-service','ts-basic-service','ts-station-food-service','ts-train-food-service') GROUP BY 1,2), n AS (SELECT service_name svc, metric, avg(value) nv, stddev(value) nsd FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('ts-food-service','ts-seat-service','ts-consign-service','ts-preserve-service','ts-route-plan-service','ts-travel-service','ts-basic-service','ts-station-food-service','ts-train-food-service') GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT a.svc, a.metric, round(n.nv,3) nv, round(a.av,3) av, round((a.av-n.nv)/nullif(n.nsd,0),1) z FROM a JOIN n USING(svc,metric) WHERE abs((a.av-n.nv)/nullif(n.nsd,0)) > 2.5 ORDER BY a.svc, abs(z) DESC

content.text: Consign's internal methods are slow across the board, not just DB calls. Next I'll check whether consign's CPU rise is steady or has an onset, and which nodes its pods run on.

input.query: SELECT service_name, attr_k8s_node_name node, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, metric, date_trunc('minute', time) t, round(avg(value),3) v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE (service_name IN ('ts-consign-service','ts-food-service') AND metric IN ('container.cpu.usage','k8s.pod.cpu_limit_utilization')) GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY 1,4,5 LIMIT 60

content.text: Consign's CPU spikes look bursty rather than sustained. The client-minus-server gap on each call is a better discriminator for network delay, so I'll compare that gap between normal and abnormal periods.

input.query: WITH pa AS (SELECT 'abn' p, c.service_name caller, s.service_name callee, (c.duration - s.duration)/1e6 gap, c.duration/1e6 cd FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client' AND s.attr_span_kind='Server'), pn AS (SELECT 'nrm' p, c.service_name caller, s.service_name callee, (c.duration - s.duration)/1e6 gap, c.duration/1e6 cd FROM normal_traces c JOIN normal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client' AND s.attr_span_kind='Server'), u AS (SELECT * FROM pa UNION ALL SELECT * FROM pn) SELECT caller, callee, sum(CASE WHEN p='nrm' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) n_nrm, round(quantile_cont(CASE WHEN p='nrm' THEN gap END,0.5),1) nrm_gap50, round(quantile_cont(CASE WHEN p='abn' THEN gap END,0.5),1) abn_gap50, sum(CASE WHEN p='abn' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) n_abn, round(quantile_cont(CASE WHEN p='nrm' THEN gap END,0.95),1) nrm_gap95, round(quantile_cont(CASE WHEN p='abn' THEN gap END,0.95),1) abn_gap95 FROM u GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING n_abn > 15 ORDER BY abn_gap95 - nrm_gap95 DESC LIMIT 25

content.text: Hubble per-connection counts show ordinary volume shifts and no clear loss on the ui-consign link. Food-service is another strong candidate, since preserve's calls into it reach 812 ms, so I'll break down food's server spans by their children.

input.query: WITH s AS (SELECT p, span_id, trace_id, duration FROM (SELECT 'abn' p, * FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'nrm', * FROM normal_traces) WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server') SELECT s.p, left(c.service_name||' '||c.span_name,80) child, c.attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95 FROM s JOIN (SELECT 'abn' pp, * FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'nrm', * FROM normal_traces) c ON c.trace_id=s.trace_id AND c.parent_span_id=s.span_id AND c.pp=s.p GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text: Food's `getAllFood` method is the slow piece (p95 61 → 205 ms). I'll check its child spans to see whether the time is in its own code or in calls it makes.

input.query: WITH g AS (SELECT 'abn' p, span_id, trace_id, duration FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' AND span_name='FoodController.getAllFood' UNION ALL SELECT 'nrm', span_id, trace_id, duration FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' AND span_name='FoodController.getAllFood') SELECT g.p, c.service_name, left(c.span_name,50) op, c.attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95 FROM g JOIN (SELECT * FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT * FROM normal_traces) c ON c.parent_span_id = g.span_id AND c.trace_id = g.trace_id GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,1

content.text: Food's client-side GET/POST spans are slower, but the matching server spans are not, which points to the transport layer. Hubble's per-connection HTTP duration metrics measure that directly, so I'll compare them between periods.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, metric, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT service_name) svc FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'nrm', metric, count(*), count(DISTINCT service_name) FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric LIKE 'hubble%' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

WITH a AS (SELECT service_name svc, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, attr_source src, attr_destination dst, avg(value) av FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric='hubble_http_request_duration_p90_seconds' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4), n AS (SELECT service_name svc, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, attr_source src, attr_destination dst, avg(value) nv FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric='hubble_http_request_duration_p90_seconds' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4) SELECT a.svc, a.src, a.dst, round(n.nv,4) nv, round(a.av,4) av, round(a.av/nullif(n.nv,0),1) ratio FROM a JOIN n USING(svc,pod,src,dst) WHERE a.av > 0.05 ORDER BY ratio DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 25

content.text: Most hubble duration rows are NaN, so I'll filter those out and compare the workload-level p90 between periods.

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT attr_source_workload s, attr_destination_workload d, avg(value) av, count(*) na FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric='hubble_http_request_duration_p90_seconds' AND NOT isnan(value) AND attr_source_workload IS NOT NULL AND attr_destination_workload IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2), n AS (SELECT attr_source_workload s, attr_destination_workload d, avg(value) nv, count(*) nn FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric='hubble_http_request_duration_p90_seconds' AND NOT isnan(value) AND attr_source_workload IS NOT NULL AND attr_destination_workload IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT a.s, a.d, round(n.nv,4) nv, round(a.av,4) av, na, nn, round(a.av/nullif(n.nv,0),2) ratio FROM a LEFT JOIN n USING(s,d) ORDER BY ratio DESC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 30

content.text: The hubble p90 for ui-dashboard → consign-service rose about 9x (0.04 → 0.35 s), the only large connection-level shift. I'll check the timing of the 503s and consign's activity per minute to see whether the failure is a sustained window.

input.query: SELECT date_trunc('minute', time) t, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND span_name LIKE '%consignservice%' AND attr_http_response_status_code=503 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ui503_consign, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND span_name LIKE '%consignservice%' AND attr_http_response_status_code=200 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ui200_consign, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-consign-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) consign_srv, round(avg(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-consign-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN duration/1e6 END),1) consign_ms, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ui_all FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

content.text: The 503s and slow consign spans cluster in the 06:37–06:38 minutes, so this looks like a transient burst. I'll check which consign metrics moved in that window, including JVM memory, GC, and threads.

input.query: WITH a AS (SELECT metric, date_trunc('minute', time) t, avg(value) v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name='ts-consign-service' GROUP BY 1,2), n AS (SELECT metric, avg(value) nv, max(value) nmax FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name='ts-consign-service' GROUP BY 1) SELECT a.metric, round(n.nv,3) nv, round(max(CASE WHEN a.t = (SELECT min(date_trunc('minute', time)) FROM abnormal_metrics) THEN a.v END),3) m0, round(max(CASE WHEN a.t = (SELECT min(date_trunc('minute', time))+INTERVAL 1 MINUTE FROM abnormal_metrics) THEN a.v END),3) m1, round(max(CASE WHEN a.t = (SELECT min(date_trunc('minute', time))+INTERVAL 2 MINUTE FROM abnormal_metrics) THEN a.v END),3) m2, round(max(CASE WHEN a.t = (SELECT min(date_trunc('minute', time))+INTERVAL 3 MINUTE FROM abnormal_metrics) THEN a.v END),3) m3, round(avg(a.v),3) aavg FROM a JOIN n USING(metric) GROUP BY a.metric, n.nv ORDER BY a.metric

content.text: Consign's working set at the first minute is only 179 MB and recovers to ~790 MB, and it emitted no server spans at 06:37. That pattern looks like a container restart. I'll check the restart counter and spans around that gap.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, date_trunc('minute', time) t, round(max(value),1) restarts, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric='k8s.container.restarts' AND service_name IN ('ts-consign-service','ts-food-service','ts-ui-dashboard','ts-seat-service') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,4 LIMIT 40
SELECT metric, count(*) n, count(DISTINCT attr_k8s_pod_name) pods, count(DISTINCT service_name) svcs FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric LIKE 'k8s.%' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, attr_k8s_container_name c, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, round(min(value),1) mn, round(max(value),1) mx, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric='k8s.container.restarts' AND (attr_k8s_container_name LIKE '%consign%' OR attr_k8s_container_name LIKE '%food%' OR attr_k8s_container_name LIKE '%ui-%' OR attr_k8s_container_name LIKE '%seat%') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'nrm', service_name, attr_k8s_container_name, attr_k8s_pod_name, round(min(value),1), round(max(value),1), count(*) FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric='k8s.container.restarts' AND (attr_k8s_container_name LIKE '%consign%' OR attr_k8s_container_name LIKE '%food%' OR attr_k8s_container_name LIKE '%ui-%' OR attr_k8s_container_name LIKE '%seat%') GROUP BY 1,2,3,4

content.text: Consign's restart counter went from 0 in the normal period to 1 and stayed there, and consign emitted no spans at 06:37. That fits a single pod restart that recovered, which is a pod_failure. Next I'll look at food's `createFoodOrder`, which slowed from ~15 to ~800 ms and sits on the preserve path.

input.query: WITH g AS (SELECT 'abn' p, span_id, trace_id, duration FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' AND span_name='FoodController.createFoodOrder' UNION ALL SELECT 'nrm', span_id, trace_id, duration FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' AND span_name='FoodController.createFoodOrder') SELECT g.p, c.service_name, left(c.span_name,60) op, c.attr_span_kind k, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95 FROM g JOIN (SELECT * FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT * FROM normal_traces) c ON c.parent_span_id = g.span_id AND c.trace_id = g.trace_id GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,3,1

transcript.content:
Other investigators, each starting fresh with the same tools, checked your draft answer: the kind of each fault, and how each fault's effect travelled. Their findings:

### `ts-consign-service`: you said `pod_failure`. They agree (confidence: medium).
Scope: Only ts-consign-service's single pod (ts-consign-service-6cfc6565f6-fphwj) is implicated. Its restart counter goes from 0 in the normal period to 1 at about 06:37:56 and stays at 1, and all of its signals (spans, logs, metrics) are absent from about 06:37:54 to 06:38:00 before resuming. The ui-dashboard consign 503s (06:37:52 to 06:38:59) never reach consign, and the container's memory and CPU were not saturated before the restart. Other services' own telemetry was not inspected beyond the consign-related queries.
Ruled out:
- `container_memory_saturated`: Container memory limit is 3221225472 bytes (3 GB) and working set peaks at about 800 MB (about 25% of limit) and plateaus; it is not pressed against the limit.
- `container_cpu_saturated`: container.cpu.usage averages 0.02 to 0.04 cores in the minutes after the restart (limit 5 cores); the only burst (max 4.58 in 06:38) is start-up activity, and there is no sustained pre-restart CPU rise.
- `process_cpu_saturated`: No sustained CPU rise on the consign container before the restart, and no jvm.* metrics exist for consign in the abnormal tables to show a process-level CPU shift.
- `jvm_heap_exhausted`: No jvm.* memory or heap metrics exist for consign in the abnormal period, so this cannot be tested directly; the container working set rising from 144 MB to 800 MB after a restart is start-up growth, not a pre-restart climb toward a limit.
- `jvm_gc_thrashing`: No jvm.* GC metrics exist for consign, so pause times cannot be measured; there is no pre-restart signal of GC churn to suggest it.
- `application_exception`: Consign's own logs in the abnormal period contain only WARN lines (queryByOrderId 'No Content', open-in-view notice) starting 06:38:32, with no ERROR lines; consign produced no logs and no spans before 06:37:54 to explain a fault inside the process.
- `network_partition`: A partition between consign and ui-dashboard would leave consign's own spans, logs and metrics flowing. Consign itself goes silent for about six seconds (its last memory sample at 06:37:53.8, first post-gap server activity around 06:38:00), and its restart counter ticks up at 06:37:56, so the outage is the consign pod, not the link.
- `http_aborted`: The 503s are complete responses with status 503 from ui-dashboard and have no child spans at all; the abort would have to occur at the consign connection, but consign is not running during the same interval, and no abort or upstream error text appears in the ui logs (the error text regex returned empty).
- `dns_lookup_failed`: No DNS-related error text appears in the ui-dashboard error logs (they are access-log entries with status 503 and no error field), and the failure is a pod gap, not a lookup failure.
Evidence:
- Consign restart counter is 1 across the whole abnormal window; normal period restart counter is 0 (max 0 over 24 samples), so exactly one restart occurred at the start of the incident.
  `SELECT attr_k8s_container_name AS container, metric, min(value) AS min_v, max(value) AS max_v, count(*) AS n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric='k8s.container.restarts' AND attr_k8s_container_name='ts-consign-service' GROUP BY 1,2`
- Consign emits no spans or logs before 06:38; its last container memory sample is at 06:37:53.8, the restart counter first reads 1 at 06:37:56.4, and the next working-set sample is at 06:37:58.8, so the gap is about six seconds around the restart.
  `SELECT 'span' src, time, service_name, span_name AS k FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-consign-service' AND time < '2025-08-19 06:38:05+00' UNION ALL SELECT 'log', time, service_name, substr(message,1,60) FROM abnormal_logs WHERE service_name='ts-consign-service' AND time < '2025-08-19 06:38:05+00' UNION ALL SELECT 'metric', time, attr_k8s_container_name, metric FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_container_name='ts-consign-service' AND metric IN ('container.memory.working_set','k8s.container.restarts') AND time < '2025-08-19 06:38:05+00' ORDER BY time LIMIT 30`
- Consign Server spans are 0 in the 06:37 minute, while ui-dashboard consign requests are 20 of 20 503s in that minute; in 06:38 consign has 12 server spans against 100 of 112 ui consign calls returning 503.
  `SELECT date_trunc('minute', time) t, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-consign-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) consign_server, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND span_name LIKE '%consignservice%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ui_consign, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND span_name LIKE '%consignservice%' AND attr_http_response_status_code=503 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ui_503, min(time) first_t, max(time) last_t FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1`
- Every 503 from ui-dashboard in the window has zero child spans (children = 0), so none of them reached consign; the first is at 06:37:54.2 and they run through 06:38:09 in this sample.
  `SELECT u.span_name, u.attr_http_response_status_code code, u.time, u.duration/1e6 ui_ms, (SELECT count(*) FROM abnormal_traces c WHERE c.parent_span_id=u.span_id) children FROM abnormal_traces u WHERE u.service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND u.span_name LIKE '%consignservice%' ORDER BY u.time LIMIT 40`
- Memory limit is 3 GB and working set tops out at about 800 MB; CPU limit is 5 cores, so the container has large headroom and no pre-restart saturation.
  `SELECT metric, min(value) mn, max(value) mx, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_container_name='ts-consign-service' AND metric IN ('k8s.container.memory_limit','k8s.container.cpu_limit','container.memory.working_set') GROUP BY 1`
- Normal period: restarts max 0, with 661 consign spans and 615 consign logs, so consign is a healthy continuously running pod before the incident.
  `SELECT 'n_restarts' k, count(*) n, max(value) mx FROM normal_metrics WHERE metric='k8s.container.restarts' AND attr_k8s_container_name='ts-consign-service' UNION ALL SELECT 'n_consign_spans', count(*), 0 FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-consign-service' UNION ALL SELECT 'n_consign_logs', count(*), 0 FROM normal_logs WHERE service_name='ts-consign-service'`

### `ts-food-service`: you said `application_method_slow`. They conclude `jvm_gc_thrashing` (confidence: low).
Scope: Affected: ts-food-service in the abnormal window. Its in-process Internal method spans slow across several methods and routes, including getAllFood, FoodOrderRepository.save, findByOrderId, Session.merge, Transaction.commit and SELECT FoodOrder, and its Server spans for both routes (GET foods and POST orders) rise. Not affected: the time is not on the wire (Food's Client calls to station-food and train-food and the caller-to-Food gap stay near normal), not in its SQL-level Client spans for ts.food_order (p50 about 0.5 ms in both periods), and not in pod CPU, memory or restarts. The lead's save p95 of 779 ms rests on one 2,984 ms call among 16; the other 15 saves take 2.5 to 44 ms. The claimed application_method_slow is not supported as a single-method fault; the evidence fits a process-wide in-process stall of unidentified origin, and no GC metric is present to confirm the mechanism.
Ruled out:
- `network_delay`: Food's Client GET spans to station-food and train-food move only from p50 8.5 to 10.4 ms, and the caller-to-Food gap is small (preserve Client POST p50 11.0 vs Food Server p50 11.9 ms in normal; the one 3-second outlier shows a 112 ms gap). The extra time is inside Food, not on the wire.
- `database_call_slow`: The SQL-level Client spans for ts.food_order are unchanged (INSERT p50 0.4 to 0.5 ms, SELECT p50 0.6 ms in both periods), and the outlier save trace has no database child spans under the 2,984 ms method.
- `http_slow`: The added time sits in Food's Internal method spans (getAllFood, findByOrderId, Session.merge, Transaction.commit) and not only in HTTP handling of one route; both Food routes and non-HTTP methods slow together, so it is not route-specific.
- `container_cpu_saturated`: k8s.pod.cpu_limit_utilization averages 0.019 in the abnormal window (max 0.194) against 0.012 normal; the container is far below its CPU limit.
- `process_cpu_saturated`: jvm.cpu.recent_utilization for the Food pod averages 0.001 abnormal and 0.001 normal, so the JVM process is not CPU-saturated.
- `jvm_heap_exhausted`: jvm.memory.used peaks at about 106 MB against a jvm.memory.limit of about 2 GB, and jvm.memory.used_after_last_gc averages about 2.3 MB, so heap is not near its limit.
- `container_memory_saturated`: k8s.pod.memory_limit_utilization is 0.254 in both periods, flat; memory does not change between normal and abnormal.
- `pod_failure`: No restart or uptime reset appears for the Food pod; its gauges have 48 samples in each period and k8s.deployment.available stays at 1.0, so the pod did not stop and recover.
- `pod_unavailable`: The Food pod keeps emitting through the whole abnormal window (48 gauge samples, same as normal) and the deployment stays available, so the instance did not stay gone.
Evidence:
- Food's in-process methods slow in the abnormal window: getAllFood Internal p50 12.5 to 23.4 ms and p95 60.8 to 204.5 ms; save p50 2.9 to 3.3 ms but p95 5.1 to 779.2 ms; findByOrderId p95 4.0 to 14.4 ms; Session.merge p95 1.6 to 10.5 ms; Transaction.commit p95 2.4 to 8.3 ms; SELECT FoodOrder p95 3.3 to 8.4 ms. Food's Server spans rise (GET foods p50 15.0 to 25.8 ms; POST orders p50 11.9 to 14.4 ms). Food's Client GET p50 goes 8.5 to 10.4 ms and Client INSERT/SELECT ts.food_order stay about 0.5 to 0.6 ms p50.
  `SELECT 'abn' AS period, attr_span_kind AS kind, span_name, count(*) AS n, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,1) AS p50_ms, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) AS p95_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', attr_span_kind, span_name, count(*), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,1), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3,1,2`
- Of 16 abnormal save calls, one takes 2,983.9 ms and the next takes 44.3 ms; the rest are 2.5 to 16.8 ms. The 779 ms p95 is therefore a single outlier, not a steady slowdown.
  `SELECT span_name, round(duration/1e6,1) AS dur_ms, attr_status_code, attr_k8s_pod_name FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' AND span_name IN ('FoodOrderRepository.save') ORDER BY duration DESC`
- In the 2,984 ms save trace, the caller's Client POST from ts-preserve-service lasts 3,119 ms and Food's Server POST /orders lasts 3,007 ms, a gap of about 112 ms. Food's FoodController.createFoodOrder (3,003.6 ms) and FoodOrderRepository.save (2,983.9 ms) carry the time, and no Food database spans appear under save, so the stall is inside the process and not on the wire.
  `WITH t AS (SELECT trace_id FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' AND span_name='FoodOrderRepository.save' ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, round(duration/1e6,1) AS dur_ms, parent_span_id IS NULL AS is_root FROM abnormal_traces WHERE trace_id IN (SELECT trace_id FROM t) ORDER BY duration DESC`
- Food logs 174 ERROR and 885 INFO lines in the abnormal window against 280 ERROR and 1,404 INFO in normal; the error count does not rise, so logs do not point to an exception path.
  `SELECT 'abn' AS period, level, count(*) AS n FROM abnormal_logs WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', level, count(*) FROM normal_logs WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' GROUP BY 1,2`
- Food pod gauges: k8s.pod.cpu_limit_utilization averages 0.019 abnormal (max 0.194) vs 0.012 normal (max 0.035); container.cpu.usage max 1.324 abnormal vs 0.19 normal; k8s.pod.memory_limit_utilization 0.254 in both; jvm.cpu.recent_utilization 0.001 in both; jvm.system.cpu.load_1m is about 117 abnormal vs 31 normal (node-level, not container). 48 samples per pod-gauge in each period, so the pod emits through the window; no restart metric appears among the gauges.
  `SELECT 'abn_gauge' AS src, metric, attr_k8s_pod_name AS pod, count(*) AS n, round(avg(value),3) AS avg_v, round(max(value),3) AS max_v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm_gauge', metric, attr_k8s_pod_name, count(*), round(avg(value),3), round(max(value),3) FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,1`
- Food sum-type metrics across both periods: jvm.memory.used max 105.7 MB against jvm.memory.limit max 2.1 GB; jvm.memory.used_after_last_gc averages 2.3 MB; jvm.thread.count max 14; k8s.pod.cpu.time and container.cpu.time are cumulative and flat (avg 350). No jvm GC pause or GC count metric is present, so GC cannot be confirmed.
  `SELECT metric, count(*) n, round(avg(value),3) avg_v, round(max(value),3) max_v FROM (SELECT metric, value, service_name FROM abnormal_metrics_sum UNION ALL SELECT metric, value, service_name FROM normal_metrics_sum) WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1`

### How the effect of `ts-consign-service` (`pod_failure`) travelled
Reasoning: The effect travelled along one route: ts-ui-dashboard calls ts-consign-service directly, and that link slowed sharply in the incident (mean duration about 36 ms to 96 ms, with no errors), so the effect reached the entry service. The link from ts-consign-price-service to ts-consign-service was not an edge: consign-price's own latency was unchanged and its calls fell only because consign itself stopped handling requests. The draft's ts-food-service and ts-preserve-service edges were not touched, because consign has no call path to either service (its only neighbours are ts-ui-dashboard and ts-consign-price-service); the food and preserve slowdowns are a separate problem.
Edges they found, from the called service to its caller:

SELECT 'abn' p, date_trunc('10 seconds', time) AS t, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-consign-service' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) consign_spans, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-consign-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) consign_server, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND span_name LIKE '%consign%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ui_consign_calls FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY t LIMIT 60

SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, attr_span_kind, span_name, count(*) n, round(quantile_cont(duration/1e6,0.5),1) p50_ms, round(quantile_cont(duration/1e6,0.95),1) p95_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE (service_name='ts-consign-service' OR (service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND span_name LIKE '%consign%')) GROUP BY ALL UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, attr_span_kind, span_name, count(*), round(quantile_cont(duration/1e6,0.5),1), round(quantile_cont(duration/1e6,0.95),1) FROM normal_traces WHERE (service_name='ts-consign-service' OR (service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND span_name LIKE '%consign%')) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2,3,4

content.text: The restart counter is 1 from the first abnormal sample, with one pod name throughout. Next I'll check uptime and resource metrics around that point, and the consign span timeline.

input.query: SELECT 'uptime_cpu_mem' src, date_trunc('minute', time) t, metric, round(avg(value),2) avg_v, round(min(value),2) mn, round(max(value),2) mx, count(*) n FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_container_name='ts-consign-service' AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.uptime','container.cpu.usage','container.memory.usage','jvm.memory.used','container.cpu.time') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY t, metric LIMIT 120

SELECT date_trunc('minute', time) t, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-consign-service' AND attr_span_kind='Server' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) consign_server, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND span_name LIKE '%consignservice%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ui_consign, sum(CASE WHEN service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND span_name LIKE '%consignservice%' AND attr_http_response_status_code=503 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) ui_503, min(time) first_t, max(time) last_t FROM abnormal_traces GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1

SELECT service_name, date_trunc('minute', time) t, count(*) n, any_value(body) sample FROM abnormal_logs WHERE service_name IN ('ts-consign-service','ts-ui-dashboard') GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY t LIMIT 40

content.text: Consign was absent for roughly 06:37:52 to 06:38:00, then came back. Its memory climbed to about 796 MB in the first two minutes. Next I'll check which metrics exist for consign, what the logs say, and what the 503 spans look like.

input.query: SELECT 'm' src, metric AS k, count(*) n, '' AS extra FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_container_name='ts-consign-service' GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'm_norm', metric, count(*), '' FROM normal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_container_name='ts-consign-service' AND metric LIKE 'k8s%' GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'log', service_name || ' | ' || coalesce(severity_text,''), count(*), left(any_value(body),160) FROM abnormal_logs WHERE service_name IN ('ts-consign-service','ts-ui-dashboard') GROUP BY service_name, severity_text ORDER BY 1,2

SELECT u.span_name, u.attr_http_response_status_code code, u.time, u.duration/1e6 ui_ms, (SELECT count(*) FROM abnormal_traces c WHERE c.parent_span_id=u.span_id) children, (SELECT string_agg(c.service_name||':'||c.span_name, ' ; ') FROM abnormal_traces c WHERE c.parent_span_id=u.span_id) child_names, u.attr_error_message FROM abnormal_traces u WHERE u.service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND u.span_name LIKE '%consignservice%' ORDER BY u.time LIMIT 40

input.query: SELECT 'abn' AS period, attr_span_kind AS kind, span_name, count(*) AS n, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,1) AS p50_ms, round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) AS p95_ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', attr_span_kind, span_name, count(*), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.5)/1e6,1), round(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-food-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 3,1,2

SELECT 'abn' AS period, c.span_name AS client_span, c.attr_peer_service AS peer, count(*) AS n, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) AS client_p50, round(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.95)/1e6,1) AS client_p95, round(quantile_cont(s.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) AS server_p50, round(quantile_cont(s.duration,0.95)/1e6,1) AS server_p95 FROM abnormal_traces c LEFT JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id = c.span_id WHERE c.service_name='ts-food-service' AND c.attr_span_kind='Client' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,3

SELECT 'abn' AS period, metric_name, count(*) AS n, round(avg(value),2) AS avg_v, round(max(value),2) AS max_v FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE '%food-service%' AND metric_name IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.time','container.cpu.usage','container.memory.usage','k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime','jvm.cpu.recent_utilization','jvm.memory.used') GROUP BY 1,2 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric_name, count(*), round(avg(value),2), round(max(value),2) FROM normal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_pod_name LIKE '%food-service%' AND metric_name IN ('k8s.pod.cpu.time','container.cpu.usage','container.memory.usage','k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime','jvm.cpu.recent_utilization','jvm.memory.used') GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1

content.text:
**Verdict: `application_method_slow` is not supported as the lead states it. The evidence points to an in-process slowdown across several Food methods, not one method.** Confidence is low. The telemetry does not identify the mechanism behind the stall.

**What supports the claim**
- The time sits inside Food, not on the wire. Food's Client spans to station-food and train-food barely move (GET p50 8.5 → 10.4 ms). The gap between the caller's Client span and Food's Server span is small (POST p50 11 ms vs Server 14 ms).
- Food's SQL-level Client spans stay fast (`INSERT ts.food_order` p50 0.4 → 0.5 ms; `SELECT ts.food_order` p50 0.6 ms in both periods). So the database and its driver are not the cause.
- The lead's figures check out: save p95 779 ms, normal 5 ms; getAllFood p95 205 ms vs 61 ms normal.

**What weakens it**
- **The save p95 is one call.** Of 16 abnormal saves, 15 take 2.5–44 ms. One takes 2,984 ms, and that single call sets the p95. Its trace has no database child spans under the method, so the time is inside the Java code. This is a stall, not a steady per-call slowdown.
- **The slowdown is not confined to one method.** getAllFood's median goes 12.5 → 23.4 ms and its p90 45 → 120 ms; it also has a 2.7 s outlier. Hibernate-level internal spans slow too: `findByOrderId` p95 4 → 14 ms, `Session.merge` 1.6 → 10.5 ms, `Transaction.commit` 2.4 → 8.3 ms, `SELECT FoodOrder` 3.3 → 8.4 ms. Several unrelated methods moving together is what a process-wide stall looks like, not a single slow method.
- **Food's own resources show no saturation.** Pod CPU limit utilization peaks at 19% and averages 2%. JVM CPU utilization is flat at ~0.1%. Heap peaks at ~106 MB against a 2 GB limit. Restarts and uptime are unchanged. So `container_cpu_saturated`, `process_cpu_saturated` and `jvm_heap_exhausted` are not supported.

**What the telemetry cannot settle**
- There are no GC pause or GC count metrics for Food, so `jvm_gc_thrashing` can neither be confirmed nor ruled out. It is the most plausible process-wide candidate, since the stalls hit everything in-process and heap use is low. But that is an inference from the pattern, not a measurement.
- Given the data, I cannot tell a method-specific fault from a process-wide stall of unknown origin.

**Recommendation:** Do not accept `application_method_slow` on the current evidence. If the lead keeps a method-level hypothesis, it needs an explanation for why Hibernate and getAllFood slow together. Pulling JVM GC pause metrics or thread-dump data for Food would separate `jvm_gc_thrashing` from a method fault.

content.text:
**Result: one propagation edge, `ts-consign-service → ts-ui-dashboard`.** The other three edges in the draft do not trace back to the fault.

**Checks**

- **Callers of `ts-consign-service`:** Parent-child joins on both periods show `ts-ui-dashboard` is the only caller. Its calls to consign went from 114 to 56 spans in the window, and the mean duration rose from 36 ms to 96 ms. No errors appeared on either side. This is the link that carried the effect to the user tier.
- **Callees of `ts-consign-service`:** The only one is `ts-consign-price-service`, which is called 13 times normally and 3 times in the incident. Its own latency is unchanged (about 11 ms). Consign's calls to it dropped because consign itself stopped handling requests. Nothing travelled from price to consign, so this link is not an edge.
- **`mysql` and hubble:** Consign's connections to `mysql` and `ts-ui-dashboard` show flow counts roughly doubling, with no drops. Nothing points to a propagated fault through them.

**Draft edges rejected**

- **`ts-food-service → ts-preserve-service`, `ts-preserve-service → ts-ui-dashboard`, `ts-food-service → ts-ui-dashboard`:** Consign has no call path to food or preserve. Consign's only neighbours are ui-dashboard and consign-price. Food's own time rose (5.7 → 26 ms) and the preserve→food calls slowed (p95 16.6 → 812 ms), but that is a separate slowdown with no link back to consign. These three edges would need a different fault source, and I did not check that source.

The survey's large metric shifts on many services (for example, page faults and filesystem usage on several services, with onset at 0 or 128 s) look like general noise. I did not treat them as evidence of propagation.

| From (called) | To (caller) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| ts-consign-service | ts-ui-dashboard | Calls 114 → 56 spans; mean 36 → 96 ms; p95 33.6 → 463.7 ms; no errors |

1. **ts-food-service → ts-preserve-service**: Calls from preserve to food went from 9.3 to 4.0 per minute, and p95 rose from 16.6 ms to 812.2 ms. Preserve's own calls to food slowed sharply, and preserve is a direct caller of food.
2. **ts-food-service → ts-ui-dashboard**: Dashboard's calls to food dropped from 369 to 241 traces in the sample, and p95 rose from 69.6 ms to 207.1 ms. This is a direct call that skips preserve.
3. **ts-preserve-service → ts-ui-dashboard**: Dashboard's calls to preserve rose in latency, p95 759.8 ms → 1,393.5 ms, and calls fell from 31.5 to 20.8 per minute. Preserve is slowed by food, and dashboard is the entry point, so this carries the effect to users.

**Draft edge rejected:**

- **ts-consign-service → ts-ui-dashboard**: Dashboard's calls to consign did slow (p95 33.6 → 463.7 ms), but this is not a route from food. Consign's only callees are consign-price-service and mysql, and neither calls food. Consign's own time also rose on its own, so this is a separate problem, not food's effect. I left it out.

**Links I checked and excluded:**

- Food's calls to station-food, train-food and travel slowed (for example, station-food p95 13.3 → 26.4 ms). These are outgoing calls from food, and the fault is an application-method slowdown inside food, not a network or outgoing-request fault. The callees' own times barely changed, so this is not food's effect travelling to them.
- Dashboard's calls to travel, travel-plan and travel2 slowed. None of those services calls food, so they are not on food's route.

**Not checked:** I did not query the hubble network metrics. I did not query whether food has any callers beyond preserve and dashboard. The trace join showed only those two.
